chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him saying: Three (types of people) have their supplication returned to them (unanswered): one of them is a man who supplicates against his wife while he is unjust to her, so it is said to him: 'Did We not place her matter in your hands?'

key_terms.أَمْرَهَا بِيَدِكَ: Her matter/affair is in your hands — referring to the husband's prerogative of divorce
key_terms.تُرَدُّ دَعْوَتُهُمْ: Their supplication is returned/rejected — a supplication that goes unanswered as a divine response
key_terms.ظَالِمٌ: Unjust, oppressive — one who commits zulm (wrongdoing/injustice) against another

ai.seo_question: What types of supplications are rejected in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that he heard this teaching — that three categories of people have their supplications rejected. Among them is a man who curses or supplicates against his wife while he himself is oppressing her. The divine response is a pointed rebuke: God reminds him that the power to end the marriage (through divorce) was placed in his hands, making his complaint against her both hypocritical and spiritually invalid. This teaching highlights the Islamic principle that supplication is not accepted when the supplicant is himself the wrongdoer with available recourse.
